response: Yes, blood pressure can change in treated hypertensive patients depending on whether it is measured by a physician or a nurse. This phenomenon is often referred to as the "white coat effect" or "white coat hypertension," where patients experience an increase in blood pressure when it is measured by a physician, possibly due to anxiety or stress. In contrast, measurements taken by a nurse may be lower, as the patient may feel more at ease. However, the difference in blood pressure readings between physician and nurse measurements can vary among individuals and may not be significant in all cases.
